entry.title: From Economics to Sports Humanities: My Academic Transition
entry.summary: From finance to economics to sports humanities and sociology — this essay traces my interdisciplinary academic journey and reflections.
entry.content:
## Why Sports Humanities and Sociology?
From a finance undergraduate degree at South China University of Technology, to a master's in economics at the University of Zurich, to a PhD in Sports Humanities and Sociology at Zhejiang University — this academic path may seem unconventional to outsiders. But for me, every step was a natural progression.
During my five years at the Sports Finance Research Center of Tsinghua PBC School of Finance, I gradually came to realize: **sport is more than an industry**. It is a social issue — one that touches on everyone's health and well-being, on innovations in social governance, and on the implementation of the "Healthy China" national strategy.
## Exercise is Medicine: A Field Worth Digging Into
"Exercise is Medicine" — the deep integration of physical activity and healthcare — is the core focus of my current research.
Traditional healthcare systems prioritize treating existing illnesses, while the unique value of sports and exercise lies in prevention. How can exercise prescriptions be incorporated into public health systems? How do we quantify the health benefits of sports participation? How can incentive mechanisms be designed to encourage more people to be physically active?
These questions are both academic problems and policy challenges. They have no ready-made answers — they can only be explored step by step through research.
## The Unique Value of an Interdisciplinary Background
My training in economics has taught me to analyze problems through a cost-benefit framework, while the perspective of sports humanities and sociology reminds me not to overlook institutions, culture, and individual experience.
This interdisciplinary training helps me, when conducting sports consumption research, to both run regression analyses and understand the cultural logic behind consumption behavior.
I look forward to weaving these two threads even more tightly together in future research.

entry.title: 从经济学到体育人文：我的学术转型之路
entry.summary: 从金融到经济学再到体育人文社会学，这篇随笔记录了我的跨学科学术旅程与思考。
entry.content:
## 为什么选择体育人文社会学？
从华南理工大学金融学本科，到苏黎世大学经济学硕士，再到浙江大学体育人文社会学博士——这条学术路径在旁人看来可能有些跳跃。但对我而言，每一步都是水到渠成的。
在清华大学五道口金融学院体育金融研究中心工作的五年里，我逐渐意识到：**体育不仅仅是产业**。它是一个社会议题，关乎每个人的健康福祉，关乎社会治理的创新，关乎"健康中国"战略的落地。
## 体卫融合：一个值得深耕的领域
"体卫融合"——即体育运动与医疗卫生的深度融合——是我目前研究的核心议题。
传统的医疗体系重在"治已病"，而体育运动的独特价值在于"治未病"。如何将运动处方纳入公共卫生体系？如何量化体育参与的健康收益？如何设计激励机制让更多人主动参与体育锻炼？
这些问题既是学术命题，也是政策难题。它们没有现成的答案，只能在研究中逐步探索。
## 跨学科背景的独特价值
我的经济学训练让我习惯于用成本-收益分析框架看待问题，而体育人文社会学的视角则提醒我不能忽略制度、文化和个体体验。
这种跨学科的训练帮助我在做体育消费研究时，既能跑回归分析，也能理解消费行为背后的文化逻辑。
期待在未来的研究中，能把这两条线索编织得更加紧密。

entry.title: How a Research Newbie Built an Academic Website in One Day
entry.summary: From double-clicking HTML files to having a dynamic academic website, all in one day. A complete record of the learning path from zero to a personal academic site — all code is ready to copy and use.
entry.content:
# How a Research Newbie Built an Academic Website in One Day
Date: 2026.05.20  |  Author: A research newbie starting from scratch  |  ~2,300 words
From "I only know how to double-click an HTML file" to "I have my own dynamic academic website" — all in one day. As a research beginner, my previous understanding of websites was limited to "a browser can open a file." Today, I decided to challenge myself: **build a personal academic website from scratch in a single day**. And I actually did it. This post documents my complete learning journey — all code can be copied and used directly, no programming background required. ## Morning: Understanding What a Webpage Actually Is ### 8:00 - 9:00 Rediscovering Three Letters: HTML, CSS, JS I always thought making a webpage required learning a very complex language. In reality, a webpage is just three things: - **HTML**: The frame of a house (positions of titles, paragraphs, images) - **CSS**: The decoration (colors, fonts, layout) - **JavaScript**: The switches (clicking buttons, showing alerts, dynamically updating content) I did a small experiment: created a `test.html` file, wrote a few lines of code in Notepad, double-clicked to open in a browser — my first "webpage" was born! It was ugly, but I understood: **HTML is just text with angle brackets, and the browser renders it into a beautiful page**. ### 9:00 - 10:00 Adding CSS to Make It Look Good I learned a bit of CSS, adding fonts, borders, and background colors to the page. Refreshed the browser — the page looked professional. I realized: **no artistic talent needed, a few lines of CSS can make an academic website look serious**. ### 10:00 - 11:00 Adding JavaScript to Make It Interactive I wanted a "Show More" button that would reveal an additional research introduction. So I learned the simplest JavaScript function. By noon, I had mastered all the basics of static webpages. But such a site has one problem — **every time you update your publication list, you have to manually edit the HTML file**. I needed a smarter approach. ## Midday: Meeting Node.js — Bringing JavaScript to the Server ### 11:30 - 12:30 What is Node.js? I used to think JavaScript could only run in a browser. Node.js breaks that limitation — it lets me run JS files directly on my computer, reading files and listening for network requests. I wrote my first Node.js program: created `hello.js`, wrote `console.log("Hello")`, then typed `node hello.js` in the terminal and saw the output. **Turns out I already had Node.js installed**, I'd just never used it. ### 13:00 - 14:00 Creating a Simple Server with Node.js I followed a tutorial and wrote 10 lines of code, ran it in the terminal, then opened my browser to `http://localhost:3000` — and saw a response. This was my first time making JavaScript act as a "backend." Although it only returned a line of text, I understood: webpages don't have to be static files; they can be generated dynamically by a program. ### 14:00 - 15:00 Encountering a Port Conflict Error and Learning to Fix It On my second run, I got an `EADDRINUSE` error. Turns out the previous server hadn't been stopped. Press Ctrl+C to terminate. **Every error is a learning opportunity** — now I know what a port is. ## Afternoon: Using Express — Building a Dynamic Site in 10 Minutes ### 15:00 - 16:00 Express Reduces Code by 60% Raw Node.js is too verbose to write. I installed Express, wrote an `app.js`, and returned dynamic HTML containing the current time. **A dynamic webpage!** Every refresh, the time updates. This made me realize: an academic website can also dynamically display the latest papers, citation counts, conference deadlines, and other real-time information. ### 16:00 - 17:00 Letting Express Handle Static Files Too I created a `public` folder, put `style.css` inside, and added one line: `app.use(express.static('public'))`. Now visiting `/style.css` in the browser automatically serves the file. **No more manual file reading**. ### 17:00 - 18:00 Final Result: A Complete Personal Academic Website I integrated everything I learned throughout the day and built a genuinely usable **personal academic website**, including: homepage (introduction, photo), research interests list, publication list (with links), and contact form. Complete code below (can be copied and used directly). ## Evening: Deploying Online for the World to See I used **Railway** (free, no credit card required) for one-click deployment: uploaded the project folder to GitHub, created a new project on Railway.app, selected "Deploy from GitHub repo" — it automatically detected Node.js and generated a `*.up.railway.app` URL. My academic website is now globally accessible! ## Complete Code (Copy and Use) The code below is a complete academic website (based on Express + EJS). Follow the comments step by step. Save the code as files, run `node app.js` on your computer, and you'll see the result. ### Project Structure ``` my_academic_site/ ├── public/ │ ├── profile.jpg (put a photo of yourself) │ └── style.css ├── views/ │ └── index.ejs ├── package.json └── app.js ``` ### 1. Initialize and Install Dependencies ```bash mkdir my_academic_site && cd my_academic_site npm init -y npm install express ejs ``` ### 2. app.js (Server Code) ```javascript const express = require('express'); const app = express(); const port = 3000; app.set('view engine', 'ejs'); app.use(express.static('public')); app.use(express.urlencoded({ extended: true })); const papers = [ { title: "Deep Learning in Image Recognition", venue: "CVPR 2024", link: "#" }, { title: "Graph Neural Networks for Recommendation Systems", venue: "KDD 2024", link: "#" } ]; app.get('/', (req, res) => { res.render('index', { name: "Zhang San", title: "PhD Candidate", institution: "School of Computer Science, XX University", interests: ["Machine Learning", "Computer Vision", "Data Mining"], papers: papers }); }); app.post('/contact', (req, res) => { console.log(req.body); res.send('

Message received, I will reply soon!

Back to Home'); }); app.listen(port, () => { console.log(`Academic site running at http://localhost:${port}`); }); ``` ### 3. views/index.ejs (Page Template) ```ejs <%= name %> - Personal Academic Homepage

<%= name %>

<%= title %>

<%= institution %>

Research Interests

    <% interests.forEach(i => { %>
  • <%= i %>
    • <% }); %>

Selected Publications

<% papers.forEach(p => { %>
<%= p.title %>
<%= p.venue %> [PDF]
<% }); %>

Contact Me

© 2025 <%= name %>

``` ### 4. public/style.css (Styles) ```css body { font-family: 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; background-color: #f8f9fa; margin: 0; padding: 20px; } .container { max-width: 800px; margin: auto; background: white; padding: 30px; border-radius: 20px; box-shadow: 0 0 20px rgba(0,0,0,0.05); } .avatar { width: 120px; height: 120px; border-radius: 50%; object-fit: cover; } h1 { color: #2c3e50; } .title { color: #3498db; font-weight: bold; } section { margin: 30px 0; padding-bottom: 20px; border-bottom: 1px solid #eee; } .paper { background: #f1f5f9; padding: 12px; margin: 10px 0; border-radius: 8px; } input, textarea, button { width: 100%; padding: 10px; margin: 8px 0; border-radius: 6px; border: 1px solid #ccc; } button { background-color: #3498db; color: white; border: none; cursor: pointer; } ``` ### 5. Run Command ```bash node app.js ``` Open your browser and visit `http://localhost:3000` to see your academic website. Swap in your own photo, update the publication list and basic info — a professional personal homepage is ready! ## Summary: What Did I Learn in One Day?
TimeMilestoneOutput
MorningHTML/CSS/JS basicsStatic personal introduction page
MiddayNode.js runtimeFirst command-line program
AfternoonExpress + template engineDynamic academic website (data-driven)
EveningDeploymentPublicly accessible personal website
> **Advice for Research Beginners** > > - Don't be afraid of code: you don't need to be a programmer — just copy, paste, and replace with your name and papers. > - Verify step by step: save and refresh your browser every few lines. Seeing results will give you tremendous confidence. > - Use templates wisely: EJS separates your data (publication list) from the interface. Future updates only require modifying one array. > - Next steps: add RSS subscriptions, Google Scholar auto-sync, a guestbook database, and more.
© 2026 A research newbie starting from scratch — You can learn to build a website in one day too

entry.title: 科研小白一天学会做个人学术网站
entry.summary: 从双击打开 HTML 到拥有动态学术网站，我花了一天。完整记录从零搭建个人学术网站的学习路径，所有代码可直接复制使用。
entry.content:
# 科研小白一天学会做个人学术网站
📅 学习日期：2026.05.20  |  ✍️ 作者：一个从零开始的科研新手  |  ⏱ 全文约 2300 字
从"只会双击打开 HTML"到"拥有自己的动态学术网站"，我花了一天。作为一名科研小白，我之前对网站的理解仅限于"浏览器能打开一个文件"。今天，我决定给自己一个挑战：**用一天时间，从零开始搭建一个个人学术网站**。最终，我真的做到了。这篇文章会完整记录我的学习路径——所有代码都可以直接复制使用，不需要任何编程基础。 ## 📘 上午：理解"网页到底是什么" ### 8:00 - 9:00 重新认识三个字母：HTML、CSS、JS 我一直以为做网页需要学一门很复杂的语言。其实，网页就三样东西： - **HTML**：房子的框架（标题、段落、图片的位置） - **CSS**：装修（颜色、字体、布局） - **JavaScript**：开关（点击按钮、弹出提示、动态更新内容） 我做了一个小实验：新建一个 `test.html`，用记事本写了几行代码，双击用浏览器打开——我的第一个"网页"诞生了！虽然丑，但我明白了：**HTML 就是带尖括号的文本，浏览器负责把它渲染成漂亮的页面**。 ### 9:00 - 10:00 加上 CSS，让页面变好看 我学了一点点 CSS，把页面加上字体、边框和背景颜色。刷新浏览器——页面变专业了。我意识到：**不需要美术天赋，几行 CSS 就能让学术网站看起来很正经**。 ### 10:00 - 11:00 加上 JavaScript，让页面"动起来" 我想让点击"显示更多"按钮时，额外显示一段研究介绍。于是学了最简单的 JavaScript 函数。一上午，我掌握了静态网页的全部基础。但这样的网站有一个问题——**每次更新论文列表，都要手动改 HTML 文件**。我需要一个更智能的方式。 ## ☕ 中午：认识 Node.js —— 让 JavaScript 跑到服务器上 ### 11:30 - 12:30 Node.js 是什么？ 我以前以为 JavaScript 只能在浏览器里运行。Node.js 打破了这个限制——它让我可以在电脑上直接运行 JS 文件，读取文件、监听网络请求。我做了第一个 Node.js 程序：新建 `hello.js`，写入 `console.log("Hello")`，然后在终端输入 `node hello.js`，看到了输出。**原来我早就安装了 Node.js**，只是从来没用过。 ### 13:00 - 14:00 用 Node.js 创建一个最简单的服务器 我照着教程写了 10 行代码，在终端运行，然后打开浏览器访问 `http://localhost:3000`——看到了响应。这是我第一次让 JavaScript 当"后台"。虽然它只是返回了一行文字，但我明白了：网页可以不是静态文件，而是由程序实时生成的。 ### 14:00 - 15:00 遇到端口占用的错误，学会了解决 运行第二次时，报错 `EADDRINUSE`。原来之前的服务器没关。按 Ctrl+C 终止就好了。**每一个错误都是学习机会**——现在我知道端口是什么了。 ## ⚡ 下午：用 Express 框架，10 分钟搭出动态网站 ### 15:00 - 16:00 Express 让代码减少 60% 原生 Node.js 写起来太啰嗦。我安装了 Express，写了一个 `app.js`，返回包含当前时间的动态 HTML。**动态网页！**每次刷新，时间都会更新。这让我意识到：学术网站也可以动态显示最新论文、引用次数、会议截止日等实时信息。 ### 16:00 - 17:00 把静态文件也交给 Express 我创建了一个 `public` 文件夹，把 `style.css` 放进去，然后代码中加一行 `app.use(express.static('public'))`。这样浏览器访问 `/style.css` 就能自动拿到文件。**再也不用手动处理文件读取了**。 ### 17:00 - 18:00 最终成果：一个完整的个人学术网站 我把一天学到的东西整合起来，做了一个真正能用的**个人学术网站**，包含：主页（介绍、照片）、研究兴趣列表、论文列表（带链接）、联系表单。完整代码见下方（可直接复制使用）。 ## 🌙 晚上：部署上线，让全世界看到 我用 **Railway**（免费，无需信用卡）一键部署：把项目文件夹上传到 GitHub，在 Railway.app 中新建项目，选择 Deploy from GitHub repo，它会自动识别 Node.js，生成一个 `*.up.railway.app` 的网址。我的学术网站现在全球可访问了！ ## 📦 完整代码（复制即用） 下面的代码是一个完整的学术网站（基于 Express + EJS），你可以按照注释一步步操作。把代码保存成文件，在电脑上运行 `node app.js` 就能看到效果。 ### 项目结构 ``` my_academic_site/ ├── public/ │ ├── profile.jpg （放一张你的照片） │ └── style.css ├── views/ │ └── index.ejs ├── package.json └── app.js ``` ### 1. 初始化并安装依赖 ```bash mkdir my_academic_site && cd my_academic_site npm init -y npm install express ejs ``` ### 2. app.js（服务器代码） ```javascript const express = require('express'); const app = express(); const port = 3000; app.set('view engine', 'ejs'); app.use(express.static('public')); app.use(express.urlencoded({ extended: true })); const papers = [ { title: "深度学习在图像识别中的应用", venue: "CVPR 2024", link: "#" }, { title: "基于图神经网络的推荐系统", venue: "KDD 2024", link: "#" } ]; app.get('/', (req, res) => { res.render('index', { name: "张三", title: "博士研究生", institution: "XX大学计算机学院", interests: ["机器学习", "计算机视觉", "数据挖掘"], papers: papers }); }); app.post('/contact', (req, res) => { console.log(req.body); res.send('

收到留言，我会尽快回复！

返回首页'); }); app.listen(port, () => { console.log(`学术网站运行在 http://localhost:${port}`); }); ``` ### 3. views/index.ejs（页面模板） ```ejs <%= name %> - 个人学术主页

<%= name %>

<%= title %>

<%= institution %>

研究兴趣

    <% interests.forEach(i => { %>
  • <%= i %>
    • <% }); %>

代表性论文

<% papers.forEach(p => { %>
<%= p.title %>
<%= p.venue %> [PDF]
<% }); %>

联系我

© 2025 <%= name %>

``` ### 4. public/style.css（样式） ```css body { font-family: 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; background-color: #f8f9fa; margin: 0; padding: 20px; } .container { max-width: 800px; margin: auto; background: white; padding: 30px; border-radius: 20px; box-shadow: 0 0 20px rgba(0,0,0,0.05); } .avatar { width: 120px; height: 120px; border-radius: 50%; object-fit: cover; } h1 { color: #2c3e50; } .title { color: #3498db; font-weight: bold; } section { margin: 30px 0; padding-bottom: 20px; border-bottom: 1px solid #eee; } .paper { background: #f1f5f9; padding: 12px; margin: 10px 0; border-radius: 8px; } input, textarea, button { width: 100%; padding: 10px; margin: 8px 0; border-radius: 6px; border: 1px solid #ccc; } button { background-color: #3498db; color: white; border: none; cursor: pointer; } ``` ### 5. 运行命令 ```bash node app.js ``` 打开浏览器访问 `http://localhost:3000` 即可看到你的学术网站。把头像换成你自己的照片，修改论文列表和基本信息，一个专业的个人主页就完成啦！ ## 📊 总结：一天究竟学到了什么？
时间里程碑产出
上午HTML/CSS/JS 基础静态个人介绍页
中午Node.js 运行环境第一个命令行程序
下午Express + 模板引擎动态学术网站（数据驱动）
晚上部署上线公网可访问的个人网站
> **给科研小白的建议** > > - 不要怕代码：我们不需要成为程序员，只需复制粘贴，替换成你的名字、论文即可。 > - 分步验证：每写几行就保存、刷新浏览器，看到效果会给你巨大信心。 > - 善用模板：EJS 让你把数据（论文列表）和界面分离，以后更新论文只需修改一个数组。 > - 下一步：可以给网站加上 RSS 订阅、Google Scholar 自动同步、留言板数据库等功能。
© 2026 一个从零开始的科研新手 — 一天也能学会做网站

entry.title: Sports Park Development: Policy Review and Outlook
entry.summary: A review of the policy evolution of sports park construction in China, analyzing current challenges and future directions.
entry.content:
## Policy Background
In 2021, seven government agencies including the National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC) jointly issued the *Guiding Opinions on Promoting Sports Park Construction*, setting a clear target of building or renovating approximately 1,000 sports parks nationwide by 2025.
This policy did not emerge in a vacuum. As "National Fitness" became a national strategy, the insufficient supply of sports facilities increasingly became a bottleneck. Traditional sports venues often lean toward large-scale, high-end facilities that fail to meet the day-to-day fitness needs of ordinary citizens.
## Findings from the National Survey
During my time at the Sports Finance Research Center at Tsinghua University, I helped organize a nationwide survey of sports parks. The survey covered multiple provinces and cities across eastern, central, and western China. We observed several noteworthy trends:
1. **Integrating Green Space with Sports**: The best sports parks are not necessarily those with the most luxurious facilities, but those that skillfully blend exercise spaces with natural landscapes. 2. **Multi-functional and Compound Needs**: Beyond traditional running tracks, basketball courts, and soccer fields, citizens increasingly demand children's play areas, senior fitness zones, and smart walking trails. 3. **Operating Models Need Urgent Innovation**: Building is easy; sustaining operations is hard. Establishing a viable long-term operating model is the key challenge.
## Policy Recommendations
Based on our survey findings, I authored a policy brief titled *Promoting Sports Park Construction to Meet National Fitness Needs*, which was adopted by the NDRC and published on its official website.
Core recommendations include: strengthening inter-agency coordination (sports, development and reform, housing and construction, natural resources), establishing diversified investment mechanisms, developing tiered construction standards, and improving operational evaluation systems.
## Looking Ahead
Sports park construction is a long-term endeavor. Upgrading from "having them at all" to "having them done well" requires sustained dialogue and collaboration among policymakers, researchers, and operators.

entry.title: 体育公园建设：政策回顾与前瞻
entry.summary: 回顾近年来中国体育公园建设政策的发展脉络，分析当前面临的挑战与未来方向。
entry.content:
## 政策背景
2021年，国家发展改革委等七部门联合印发《关于推进体育公园建设的指导意见》，明确提出到2025年全国新建或改扩建1000个左右体育公园的目标。
这一政策的出台并非偶然。随着全民健身上升为国家战略，体育场地设施的供给不足日益成为制约因素。传统的体育场馆往往"高大上"有余而"接地气"不足，难以满足普通市民日常健身需求。
## 全国调研的发现
在清华大学体育金融研究中心工作期间，我参与组织了全国体育公园调研。调研覆盖了东中西部多个省市，我们看到了许多值得关注的趋势：
1. **绿色与体育的融合**：最好的体育公园不一定是设施最奢华的，而是那些将运动空间与自然景观巧妙结合的。 2. **多功能复合需求**：除了传统的跑步、篮球、足球场地，市民对儿童游乐、老年健身、智慧步道的需求日益强烈。 3. **运营模式亟待创新**：建设容易运维难，如何建立可持续的运营模式是关键挑战。
## 政策建议
基于调研发现，我撰写的政策解读《推进体育公园建设 满足全民健身需求》被国家发展改革委采纳并刊登在官方网站。
核心建议包括：加强部门协同（体育、发改、住建、自然资源）、建立多元化投入机制、制定分层次的建设标准、完善运营考核体系。
## 展望
体育公园建设是一个长期工程。从"有没有"到"好不好"的升级，需要政策制定者、研究者、运营者的持续对话与协作。
